region: Pacific Oceania — Micronesia, Polynesia & Hawaii
description: Lives in the white-water surge zone of exposed outer reefs, grazing filamentous algae from rock. The orange teardrop around the tail spine grows larger with age.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea & Bali
description: Forms large grazing aggregations on shallow reef flats and outer slopes of the Indian Ocean. Often intolerant of other tangs and prone to marine ich in captivity.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to southern Japan
description: A chocolate-brown grazer with a white band running from the eye to the mouth and orange stripes along the bases of the dorsal and anal fins. Lives on shallow, wave-swept reef flats.

region: Indo-Pacific to the eastern Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Hawaii & Mexico
description: Sold as the Gold Rim Tang for the thin yellow lines along its fin bases; a small white cheek spot sits below the eye. Grazes algae on clear-water outer reefs.

region: Western Atlantic — New York & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean; Ascension
description: Juveniles are bright yellow and pass through a blue-with-yellow-tail stage before turning all blue. Adults graze turf algae in roving schools that swamp territorial damselfish.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Marquesas & Ryukyu Islands
description: Holds feeding territories and harems on surge-battered reef crests, chasing off other grazers. Its tail spine is venomous and it is one of the most aggressive surgeonfishes in aquaria.

region: Red Sea & Arabian Gulf
description: Defends algae gardens on the outer edges of Red Sea reefs where waves break. Its thin black lines and orange tail spine make it striking, but it is among the most aggressive tangs in captivity.

region: Western & central Pacific, eastern Indian Ocean
description: Adults bear an orange bar outlined in dark blue behind the eye; juveniles are plain yellow. Feeds on diatom and detritus films over sand and rubble.

region: Indo-Pacific — Seychelles to the Marquesas & southern Japan
description: Juveniles mimic Centropyge angelfishes (yellow, half-black or Eibl's pattern) and are sold as Mimic Tangs. Adults turn brown with an orange patch around the gill opening and a yellow-edged tail.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea & Hawaii
description: One of the most abundant surgeonfishes on shallow reef flats, also called the Lavender Tang; tiny orange spots dot its head. Gathers in huge spawning aggregations at dusk.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — East Africa to Panama
description: Forms large roving schools that overwhelm territorial damselfish to graze their algae. Pale greenish-white with five narrow black bars, the first through the eye.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus
description: Named for the black elongate streak behind the eye; a second black streak runs forward from the tail spine. Feeds on algal and detrital films over sand next to reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Line Islands
description: Tan with fine wavy blue lines, a yellow-orange band behind the eye and a blue tail sprinkled with black spots. Grazes diatom and detritus films off sand, and grows large.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea
description: A plankton-feeding surgeonfish that schools in midwater along steep, often turbid reef slopes. It can switch from dark brown to pale blue in seconds; two yellow lines run forward from the eye.

region: Atlantic — Massachusetts to Brazil incl. Caribbean; West Africa
description: Grey-brown with about ten narrow dark vertical bars and a dark-edged tail spine. Grazes turf algae in mixed schools with Atlantic blue tangs and ocean surgeons.

region: Western South Atlantic — Brazil, Ascension & St Helena
description: A plain tan-grey Atlantic surgeonfish with a pale band around the tail base and a pale-edged, deeply concave tail; Caribbean fish were split off as A. tractus in 2015. Grazes algae over reef and seagrass edges.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to Sri Lanka & western Indonesia
description: Brown with two dark, blue-edged dashes behind the eye and a blue-ringed black patch around the tail spine. Juveniles are orange-yellow.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific
description: The largest Acanthurus: purplish-grey with yellow pectoral fins and a yellow patch in front of the eye. Feeds on films of diatoms and detritus over sand; mainly a public-aquarium fish.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Dark grey-brown with a yellow streak behind the eye and a white ring around the base of the tail. Grazes algal films off sand and dead coral.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: A plankton-picking surgeonfish that hovers in midwater along drop-offs instead of grazing rock. Uniform chocolate brown with a contrasting white tail.

region: Pacific (antitropical) — Hawaii, southern Japan, Marianas, Polynesia & Easter Island
description: Brown with a white-edged dark bar curving down behind the eye and a pale ring before the tail. Grazes algae in schools on shallow, surge-swept rocky reefs, mostly in subtropical waters.

region: Indo-Pacific — Mauritius to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Lives in the turbulent white water of reef fronts, where its white spots may blend with bubbles. Dark brown with two white bars and yellow pelvic fins.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Samoa
description: Named for the orange ring ("socket") around its tail spine; otherwise dark grey-brown with a pale band at the base of the tail. Long confused with A. bariene.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Red Sea sister species of the epaulette surgeonfish: dark brown to black with a black streak behind the eye and a white band across the base of the tail.

region: Pacific — Indonesia to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Raises enormous dorsal and anal fins to look twice its size when threatened. Tan and brown vertical bands cover the body, and the head is dotted with pale yellow spots.

region: Red Sea & Indian Ocean — East Africa to India & Indonesia
description: Indian Ocean counterpart of the Pacific sailfin, with fine yellow vertical lines between its dark bars and a head covered in pale spots. Juveniles often hide among branching corals.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Also called the Brown or Two-tone Tang: tan in front, darkening to chocolate toward the tail, with a white tail spine. Small groups graze filamentous algae on reef slopes.

region: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden & Arabian Gulf
description: Deep purple-blue with a bright yellow tail and pectoral fins and fine dark speckles on the head. Grazes algae on Red Sea reefs and is notably intolerant of other Zebrasoma.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Mozambique, Madagascar, Mauritius & Réunion
description: Dark brownish-black peppered with white spots and finished with a yellow tail. Restricted to the western Indian Ocean and one of the most expensive tangs in the trade.

region: South Pacific — Society, Tuamotu, Marquesas, Line & Pitcairn Islands
description: An all-black Zebrasoma with a markedly long snout from remote Polynesian islands; the snout lengthens with age. Rare and costly in the trade.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Uses comb-like bristle teeth to brush diatoms and detritus off rock rather than biting algae. Brown with fine blue lines and a bright yellow ring around the eye.

region: Western central Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Solomons
description: A bristletooth from sheltered lagoon reefs, named for the Gulf of Tomini in Sulawesi. Grey-brown with orange-red rear dorsal and anal fins edged in white.

region: Pacific — Hawaii, Micronesia & Polynesia
description: Juveniles are orange with blue chevron lines; adults turn almost black with fine olive pinstripes. Brushes diatom film off reef rock with flexible bristle teeth.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus
description: Brown with fine blue lines, a blue ring around the eye and a small black spot at the rear base of both the dorsal and anal fins. Juveniles have a yellow tail.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea
description: One of the most abundant reef surgeonfishes, sweeping detritus and diatoms from dead coral. Dark olive-brown with many thin blue-grey lines and tiny orange dots on the head.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Indian Ocean twin of the Kole Tang: dark grey-brown with fine blue dots and a golden ring around the eye. Juveniles are sometimes bright yellow.

region: Pacific — Indonesia & southern Japan to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: A hornless unicornfish with a yellow-edged dark face mask, orange lips and two orange keeled plates on each side of the tail stalk. Browses leafy brown algae; males grow trailing tail streamers.

region: Indian Ocean & Red Sea — East Africa to Bali
description: The Indian Ocean sister of the orangespine unicornfish, sold as the Blonde Naso for its yellow-orange dorsal fin. Grazes leafy brown algae over reef flats.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Adults grow a short bony horn on the forehead and carry two blue keeled plates on the tail stalk. Browses tough brown algae in schools on shallow reefs; a public-aquarium species.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Marquesas & southern Japan
description: Covered in blue dots and vertical blue lines that brighten instantly when it visits a cleaning station; adults develop a bulbous snout. Feeds on zooplankton in midwater off reef slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Adults grow a long, tapering horn that projects forward over the mouth. Juveniles graze algae, while adults switch to feeding on zooplankton in midwater along reef slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: A slender, hornless unicornfish that schools above steep outer reef slopes feeding on zooplankton. Males can flash a pale blue courtship pattern within seconds.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to El Salvador
description: Grey peppered with black spots, with a bright yellow tail and a row of black bony plates along the tail stalk. Travels the rocky reefs of the Gulf of California in large grazing schools.

region: Eastern Pacific — Costa Rica to Ecuador, Cocos & Galápagos Islands
description: Grey with two dark bars across the head and a yellow tail; the black keeled plates on its tail stalk give it its name. Forms large grazing schools around the Galápagos.

region: Southwest Pacific — eastern Australia, Lord Howe Island & New Caledonia
description: Grey with scattered yellow spots and short yellow lines, and three or four black plates on the tail stalk. A subtropical grazer often seen in schools on rocky reefs around Sydney.

region: Eastern Australia — southern Queensland to New South Wales
description: A large, plain grey to grey-brown surgeonfish with a row of five or six black bony plates along the tail stalk. Schools over shallow rocky reefs and kelp edges.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & southern China
description: A grey sawtail with four or five black keeled plates on the tail stalk, abundant on rocky reefs of southern Japan. Schools graze algae in the cool, temperate-subtropical water.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to New Caledonia & the Marshall Islands
description: Pairs browse algae among branching corals; the fin spines are venomous. When frightened or asleep it fades to a mottled brown and raises its dorsal spines.

region: Western Pacific — Philippines, Ryukyu Islands & Great Barrier Reef
description: Identical to the common foxface except for a black blotch on the upper flank; some authors treat it as a colour form of S. vulpinus. Browses algae in pairs among corals.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Andaman Sea (Thailand & Myanmar)
description: Andaman Sea endemic with the foxface's black-and-white face plus a broad black saddle across the middle of the back. Pairs graze algae among corals.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to the Great Barrier Reef & Fiji
description: Yellow overlaid with wavy blue lines and two dark diagonal bars on the head. Lives in pairs on coastal reefs, grazing algae and seagrass.

region: Indo-West Pacific — India & Sri Lanka to the Philippines & northern Australia
description: Yellow with blue-spotted head and back and two dark, blue-edged diagonal bars across the head. Pairs graze algae on coastal reefs and around mangroves.

region: Indian Ocean incl. Red Sea — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Pale grey-white densely covered with dark brown spots, with a bright yellow margin to the tail and rear dorsal fin. Pairs patrol coral reefs grazing algae.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Philippines & Palau
description: Blue-grey with dense golden-orange spots and a bright yellow blotch below the rear of the dorsal fin. Tolerates brackish estuaries and mangroves and is farmed for food in Southeast Asia.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Seychelles to New Caledonia
description: Golden yellow-orange covered in small blue spots, with a dark triangular patch below the eye. Lives in pairs among live coral, grazing algae.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Kiribati
description: Yellow with blue wavy lines and spots, and a dark diagonal mask running through the eye. Pairs live among corals on clear lagoon and seaward reefs.

region: Southwest Pacific — Fiji & New Caledonia
description: Dark chocolate-brown over the front two-thirds and bright yellow at the rear and tail. Restricted to Fiji and New Caledonia, where pairs browse algae among coral.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Sri Lanka to New Caledonia & Vanuatu
description: Blue-grey with wavy golden lines and a yellow blotch below the rear dorsal fin. Forms schools in shallow lagoons and seagrass beds, grazing algae.

region: Western Pacific — Ryukyu Islands to the Great Barrier Reef & Samoa
description: Dusky blue-grey densely covered with small golden-orange spots. Adults live in pairs on coral reefs, grazing algae.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Arabian Gulf to Indonesia & Vanuatu
description: Blue-grey with pale spots on the upper body that turn into wavy lines lower down, and a dark tail. Schools in turbid coastal waters and estuaries.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — East Africa to Mexico
description: Sole member of its family, with a tubular snout, broad black bands and a long white dorsal streamer. Feeds largely on sponges and tunicates, which makes it notoriously hard to keep.

region: Pacific Oceania — Palau & the Marshall Islands to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Brilliant red-orange with four or five black bars and blue-black-tipped dorsal and anal fins. Lives in small harems among rubble and coral heads; like all dwarf angels it begins life female.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Samoa & southern Japan
description: Bright yellow front and tail with a royal-blue rear body and a blue saddle over the eye. Forms harems in rubble zones and lagoons.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Orange flanks crossed by fine dark blue-purple bars, under a deep-blue back and fins. Lives among rubble and coral on lagoon and outer reefs; among the hardiest dwarf angels.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Sri Lanka to Indonesia & northwest Australia
description: Pale grey crossed by fine orange vertical lines, darkening to black at the rear, with a gold ring around the eye. Juvenile Acanthurus pyroferus and A. tristis mimic its colours.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & the Philippines
description: Rusty orange-brown peppered with small dark spots, with electric-blue edges on the dorsal and anal fins. Lives in rubble and crevices on shallow reefs.

region: Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Easter Island & the Marshall Islands
description: Lemon-yellow with electric-blue rings around the eyes and blue edges on the gill cover and fins. Notorious for nipping clam mantles and large-polyp stony corals.

region: Pacific — Taiwan & the Philippines to the Tuamotus
description: All yellow, lacking the blue eye ring and fin edges of the lemonpeel; some show a dusky smudge behind the eye. Lives among rubble on outer reef slopes.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Hawaiian endemic with an orange-red head and forebody grading into a dark blue rear, all crossed by fine wavy dark lines. Shy, staying close to coral rubble.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida, Gulf of Mexico & Caribbean
description: Among the smallest marine angelfishes: deep blue with a yellow-orange face and chest and a blue eye ring. Lives in rubble on deeper reefs, often below 30 m.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa, Madagascar & the Seychelles
description: Deep blue with an orange-yellow head and back and a clear tail. A small, comparatively peaceful dwarf angel of rubble slopes.

region: Western Atlantic — southern Caribbean to Brazil
description: Blue body with an orange band running from the snout along the back; unlike the African flameback its tail is blue. Lives in rubble on deeper reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island to the Marshall Islands & Vanuatu
description: Pale cream at the front blending to black at the rear, with an orange spot behind the gill cover. Commonly hybridizes with Eibl's and lemonpeel angelfishes.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island to New Caledonia & southern Japan
description: Blue-black with a single white vertical blotch on the flank, likened to a keyhole, and yellow pelvic fins. Lives among rubble on lagoon and outer reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Solomon Islands & GBR
description: Entirely jet-black, a secretive dwarf angel of rubble slopes and coral thickets. Less inclined to nip corals than most of its relatives.

region: Indian Ocean incl. Red Sea — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Dark brown with faint vertical bars, a black spot behind the gill and blue-edged fins. Abundant in rubble and coral crevices and very hardy in aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to the Great Barrier Reef & Samoa
description: Orange-gold covered in fine dark vertical lines, with thin blue fin edges. Extremely shy, rarely leaving deep crevices on rubble slopes.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Ogasawara Islands & Midway
description: Orange head and forebody grading into a blue rear, sprinkled with blue spots, and an orange-yellow tail. One of the largest Centropyge, from cool subtropical reefs.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Christmas & Cocos-Keeling Islands
description: Yellow front and tail with a royal-blue rear body and a blue ring around the eye. Known only from Christmas and Cocos-Keeling islands.

region: South Atlantic — Ascension Island
description: Ascension Island endemic: deep blue with a yellow-orange band running from the snout over the back and into the dorsal fin. Lives on rubble below about 15 m.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: A small Hawaiian dwarf angel, orange with a darker rear, a dark spot behind the gill and blue-lined dorsal and anal fins. Lives in rubble on deeper reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling, Palau, Guam & Fiji
description: A deep-reef dwarf angel, yellow with a large blue-violet saddle across the back and dorsal fin and a blue eye ring. Usually found below 30 m in caves on steep walls.

region: South Pacific — Cook Islands (Rarotonga)
description: Lemon-yellow with a large black spot on the upper flank, found on deep walls beyond 100 m; named for the nitrogen narcosis divers risk collecting it. Very rare in the trade.

region: Indian Ocean — Sri Lanka, the Maldives & Andaman Sea
description: Dark blue-black with faint darker lines and contrasting bright yellow pectoral fins. Lives among rubble on reef slopes of the central Indian Ocean.

region: Western Pacific — Mariana & Ogasawara Islands
description: Orange with irregular darker vertical bars and blue-edged dorsal and anal fins, sometimes sold as the Mango Angelfish. Hybridizes with the flame angelfish where they overlap.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to the Society Islands & southern Japan
description: Pale yellow-white with bold black vertical bars and yellow pelvic fins. Secretive, hiding deep in caves and crevices of reef walls; often slow to feed in aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & the Philippines
description: Golden yellow with a purple-blue back, mask and fins. A deep-reef species living in caves on steep walls, rarely collected.

region: South Pacific — Cook Islands (Rarotonga) & French Polynesia
description: Red-orange with five crisp white vertical bars, living in caves on walls deeper than 50 m. One of the most expensive aquarium fishes ever sold.

region: Western Pacific — Malaysia & Indonesia to Vanuatu & southern Japan
description: A silvery planktivore striped in black that feeds in midwater above steep slopes, unlike most angelfishes. Males are larger and carry a yellow spot on the forehead.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Fiji & southern Japan
description: A swallowtail angel with strong sexual dichromatism: females are yellow-backed with black-edged tail lobes, while males are pale blue-grey with fine black bars and a black chest spot.

region: Western & central Pacific — Taiwan & southern Japan to the Tuamotus & New Caledonia
description: Females are pale blue with black-edged dorsal fin and tail lobes and a dark cap; males are bluer with black horizontal lines on the lower flanks. Feeds on plankton along deep walls.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling & Indonesia to the Marshall & Society Islands
description: Females are silvery-white with black stripes along the back and from eye to tail; males are pale grey with an orange-yellow stripe along the flank and dorsal fin. A deep-water planktivore.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan, Ogasawara Islands & the northern Philippines
description: Males have a yellow-orange head and back and fine black bars on the mid-flank; females are pale grey with a dark cap and black-edged tail lobes. Feeds on plankton on cool subtropical reefs.

region: Hawaiian Islands (mostly Northwestern Hawaiian Islands) & Midway
description: A deep-water Hawaiian endemic: females are white with a black face mask and black pelvic fins, while males have a yellow-orange mask and fin trim. One of the most sought-after angelfishes.

region: Western Indian Ocean & Red Sea — East Africa to the Maldives
description: Males are pale blue-grey with many thin black vertical bars and a black-lined lyre tail; females are plain pale blue with a dark cap and black-edged tail lobes. Harems feed on plankton along deep slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Adults are striped yellow on blue with a black mask and a dark, blue-edged shoulder patch; juveniles have concentric white rings on blue and transform at 8–12 cm. Grunts audibly when disturbed.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to New Guinea & southern Japan
description: Orange-brown with arching blue lines across the body and a blue ring behind the gill cover; the tail is white. Lives in pairs or small groups on coastal reefs and around wrecks.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Fiji & southern Japan
description: Named for the juvenile's white semicircles, said to resemble Arabic script; adults turn greenish-brown with blue-edged fins and blue spots on the face. Hardy and adaptable in large aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to New Guinea & the Great Barrier Reef
description: Orange-yellow above with blue-spotted scales and a blue-black lower body outlined in electric blue that sweeps from the face to the tail. Lives on coral-rich lagoon reefs.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Maldives to Vanuatu & southern Japan
description: A blue face mesh with a yellow mask over the eyes, yellow pectoral fins and tail, and a black eyespot at the rear of the dorsal fin. Each body scale is edged in yellow.
